text:
Review scope: all files currently present under `/work`.

Quality score: **6.0/10**. The project is small, readable, and has a decent fixture-based test suite. The core happy path works: `pytest -q` reports **58 passed**. But I would not call it production-ready because parser hardening and ingest lifecycle semantics are weak.

**Concrete Issues**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | `evalmerge/ingest.py` | 72-89 | Re-ingesting a different dataset leaves stale `results` and `model_aliases` rows from prior ingests. |
| high | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 114, 205, 269 | Non-finite scores like `NaN` are accepted as numeric and can crash ingest with SQLite `NOT NULL` failures. |
| medium | `evalmerge/cli.py` | 44-47 | Empty-directory ingest mutates/creates the DB before returning an error. |
| medium | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 203-205 | Format B crashes when `metrics` is a truthy non-object instead of producing a structured warning. |
| medium | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 254 | Malformed Format C XML raises `ParseError` and aborts the whole ingest pass. |
| medium | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 254 | Untrusted XML is parsed with stdlib `ElementTree`; use `defusedxml` or equivalent limits for XML DoS hardening. |
| medium | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 87, 173, 254 | Parsers load entire input files/trees into memory, which will not scale for large eval exports. |
| medium | `evalmerge/parsers.py` | 88-91 | Format A processes CSV line-by-line, so valid quoted multiline CSV fields are misparsed as bad rows. |
| medium | `evalmerge/ingest.py` | 80-85 | Duplicate IDs in sources A/C are silently treated as corrections even though correction semantics are only documented for B. |
| low | `evalmerge/cli.py` | 61-67 | `report` accepts any existing empty SQLite file and initializes schema, making “run ingest first” enforcement weak. |
| low | `pyproject.toml` | 5-19 | No dev/test dependency metadata or lint/type-check config, so contributor setup and review automation are underspecified. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **~220 lines** total, including parser validation/streaming changes, ingest replacement semantics, CLI ordering fixes, and new regression tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this in a PR review as-is.**

issues.description: Re-ingesting a different dataset leaves stale results and model_aliases rows from prior ingests.
Non-finite scores like NaN are accepted as numeric and can crash ingest with SQLite NOT NULL failures.
Empty-directory ingest mutates or creates the database before returning an error.
Format B crashes when metrics is a truthy non-object instead of producing a structured warning.
Malformed Format C XML raises ParseError and aborts the whole ingest pass.
Untrusted XML is parsed with stdlib ElementTree without XML DoS hardening.
Parsers load entire input files or XML trees into memory instead of streaming.
Format A processes CSV line-by-line, so valid quoted multiline CSV fields are misparsed.
Duplicate IDs in sources A and C are silently treated as corrections even though only B documents correction semantics.
Report accepts any existing empty SQLite file and initializes schema, weakening run-ingest-first validation.
No dev/test dependency metadata or lint/type-check configuration is defined.
